questions.question: What are Enumerable and Comparable in Ruby?
questions.title: Enumerable and Comparable
questions.direct_answer: Enumerable and Comparable are mixins that add collection and sorting behavior to a class. Enumerable gives each, map, select, reduce, sort, min/max, count, include? — but your class must define `each` (Enumerable calls it). Comparable gives <, >, ==, between?, sort (via <=>) — your class must define the spaceship operator `<=>` (returns -1, 0, or 1). Example: class Box; include Enumerable; def each(&b); @items.each(&b); end; end — now Box has map/select/reduce. class Length; include Comparable; attr_reader :m; def <=>(other); m <=> other.m; end; end — now Length supports <, >, sort, min/max. Both let you compose behavior instead of rewriting it: define one method (each or <=>), get dozens free. Use Enumerable for collections, Comparable for things with a natural order.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you know Enumerable needs `each` defined and Comparable needs `<=>` defined, and each gives many methods free.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Including Enumerable without defining `each` (raises/returns nil), or Comparable without `<=>`.
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Enumerable needs `each` (gives map/select/reduce/sort). Comparable needs `<=>` (gives </>/==/between?/sort). Mixins = define one, get many free.

```ruby
# Enumerable: define `each` -> get map/select/reduce/sort/count free
class Box
  include Enumerable
  def initialize(*items); @items = items; end
  def each(&b); @items.each(&b); end   # REQUIRED by Enumerable
end

b.map { |n| n * 2 }      # [2, 4, 6]
b.select { |n| n > 1 }   # [2, 3]
b.reduce(:+)            # 6
b.sort                  # [1, 2, 3]
b.count                 # 3
b.include?(2)          # true

# Comparable: define `<=>` -> get </>/==/between?/sort/clamp
class Length
  include Comparable
  attr_reader :m
  def initialize(m); @m = m; end
  def <=>(other); @m <=> other.m; end   # REQUIRED by Comparable
end
a = Length.new(2); b2 = Length.new(5)
a < b2                  # true
a > b2                  # false
a == Length.new(2)      # true
a.between?(b2, b2)      # false
[a, b2].sort           # [Length 2, Length 5]
[a, b2].min            # Length 2

# Define ONE method, get DOZENS free. Enumerable for collections; Comparable for order.
```
